k1.author: worker-B
k1.text: svc.apply(app) is still the submission endpoint in API v2 (response shape changed; see k11).

k10.author: worker-B
k10.text: The network referral rule only overrides an "issue" decision to queue_review; it must NOT convert a partner "decline" into queue_review — a decline stays a decline.

k11.author: worker-B
k11.text: API v2 outcome values are "approved", "declined", "manual_review" (NOT v1's "approve"/"decline"/"refer").

k12.author: worker-B
k12.text: In API v2 the limit field is `credit_limit` inside `result`, not top-level `limit`.

k2.author: worker-B
k2.quote: svc.apply now returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.
k2.text: API v2 response: svc.apply returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved"|"declined"|"manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.

k3.author: seed
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}; action `issue` uses the returned limit, action `decline` has limit 0.

k4.author: worker-B
k4.quote: outcome manual_review replaces refer and is handled as in spec section 3.
k4.text: Decision mapping (API v2): approved -> issue with credit_limit; declined -> decline; manual_review -> queue_review.

k5.author: worker-B
k5.quote: For every partner in the network, whatever the partner decided, an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k5.text: Network referral rule (all partners): a self_employed applicant with requested_limit above 6000 must be queue_review instead of issued, regardless of the partner's decision; a decline stays a decline.

k6.author: worker-B
k6.quote: Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k6.text: svc.apply application fields are: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.

k7.author: worker-B
k7.text: For unknown/missing decision values, the safe default is queue_review (manual review), not decline or issue.

k8.author: worker-B
k8.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review)
k8.text: The network referral rule uses strict "above 6000" (> 6000) on requested_limit; exactly 6000 does NOT trigger manual review.

k9.author: worker-B
k9.text: queue_review and decline responses always carry limit 0; only issue carries a non-zero limit (the limit returned by svc.apply).
